title: Jensen Huang Steps Down as Nvidia CEO After 33 Years
dek: The founder left the chip giant's top job and its board as scrutiny of his personal relationships and possible security risks grew. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO.
body: Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and led it for 33 years, stepped down as chief executive on Thursday, 12 November. He also left the company's board. Nvidia did not give a reason for the move.

His exit followed days of scrutiny. Huang admitted last weekend that he had been unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family and to Nvidia staff. Reports since then have raised questions about his relationships, including one with a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore company that bought billions of dollars of Nvidia AI chips and is alleged to have links to Chinese intelligence.

Nvidia's board has opened an independent investigation and says it has no reason to believe national security was compromised. There is no established evidence that Huang knowingly helped Beijing or that company secrets were leaked.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress, at Nvidia since 2013, is now interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. Nvidia's shares fell more than 14% at one point on Thursday before recovering some ground, and US lawmakers have asked Huang to testify in December.

title: Coachella 2027: Dua Lipa, SZA, Tame Impala and Daddy Yankee Headline as Ayra Starr Makes the Cut
dek: The desert festival's next edition runs across two weekends in April, with Nigeria's Ayra Starr booked for Sunday.
body: Coachella revealed its 2027 lineup on Tuesday, 10 November. Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA top the bill, and Daddy Yankee joins as a fourth headliner with a special production.

The festival runs over two weekends in Indio, California: 9 to 11 April and 16 to 18 April 2027. Madonna, Kehlani, Steve Lacy, Leon Thomas, Victoria Monét, Jorja Smith, JISOO, Don Toliver and Phoebe Bridgers are also on the poster.
Nigerian Afrobeats star Ayra Starr is on the Sunday lineup, and British-Nigerian singer Odeal plays Saturday.
Presale passes went on sale on Thursday and general passes on Friday. YouTube returns as the festival's official streaming partner.

title: Arokodare Double Fires Super Eagles Past Tanzania in Uyo
dek: Nigeria won 3-1 in the first of two AFCON 2027 qualifiers against Tanzania this week.
body: Nigeria beat Tanzania 3-1 at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo on Friday, 13 November, in an AFCON 2027 qualifier.

Alhassan Yusuf put the Super Eagles ahead in the third minute. Tanzania drew level through Msanga in the 36th minute, but Tolu Arokodare scored twice after the break, in the 52nd and 60th minutes, to settle it.
Coach Eric Chelle's squad meets Tanzania again in the return leg on Tuesday, 17 November.

title: Democrats Take Control of Both Houses of Congress in the US Midterms
dek: The Associated Press projected Democratic majorities in the Senate and the House after a night of flips across the map.
body: Democrats won control of both the US Senate and the House of Representatives in the 3 November midterm elections, according to projections by the Associated Press.

By early Wednesday, 4 November, Democrats had flipped seven Republican-held Senate seats and more than two dozen House seats. They needed a net gain of four seats in the Senate and three in the House to take each majority.
Projected Democratic Senate winners included James Talarico in Texas, Roy Cooper in North Carolina, Sherrod Brown in Ohio and Troy Jackson in Maine. Jon Ossoff held his seat in Georgia.
The new Congress takes office in January. Republicans keep the White House, so the results set up a divided government for the final two years of President Donald Trump's term.

title: Dangote Refinery IPO Draws About $4.1 Billion in Bids
dek: Demand for shares in Africa's biggest refinery came in at roughly three times the target, setting up a landmark listing in Lagos.
body: The Dangote refinery's initial public offering has drawn about $4.1 billion (around N5.85 trillion) in share applications, roughly three times what it set out to raise. Bloomberg called it Africa's top IPO.
The subscription period was extended, and the listing on the Nigerian Exchange is now expected in December.
Analysts at Nairametrics say the listing, along with a steadier naira and strong foreign reserves, could push the total value of Nigerian stocks past N230 trillion by the end of the year.

title: Godzilla Minus Zero Sets a North American Record With $31.6 Million Debut
dek: The Japanese sequel opened at No. 1, the biggest start ever for a foreign-language live-action film other than The Passion of the Christ.
body: Godzilla Minus Zero topped the North American box office on the weekend of 6 to 8 November with an estimated $31.6 million, according to studio figures reported by the Associated Press.

That beat the previous foreign-language live-action record held by Hero ($17.9 million). Among live-action foreign-language films, only The Passion of the Christ opened bigger, with $83.8 million in 2004.
The film cost under $20 million to make and has strong reviews, with 90% on Rotten Tomatoes and an A CinemaScore. Warner Bros.' The Cat in the Hat came second with $20.5 million.
Overall ticket sales rose nearly 97% from the slow Halloween weekend before it.

title: Google Opens Preorders for Its Gemini Smart Glasses
dek: Frames from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster start at $395, with the glasses going on sale on 10 December.
body: Google opened preorders on 12 November for smart glasses built around its Gemini AI assistant, made with partners Warby Parker, Gentle Monster and Samsung. They go on sale on 10 December.
Warby Parker offers three frames starting at $395, and Gentle Monster offers six designs from $449. Google lists a 12-megapixel camera and up to nine hours of battery life, depending on use.

At launch the glasses are limited to eligible Google accounts in the United States and South Korea. Privacy features include a light that shows when the camera is recording and a physical power-off switch.

title: Van Hollen Challenges Schumer for Senate Democratic Leader
dek: The Maryland senator says the party needs new leadership as Democrats prepare to take the Senate majority.
body: Maryland Democrat Chris Van Hollen said on 12 November that he will challenge Chuck Schumer to lead Senate Democrats in the new Congress, when the party will hold the majority after the midterms.
In a social media post, Van Hollen said the party needs "new leadership", adding that the challenge "isn't about any one person". Schumer has led Senate Democrats since 2017.
Senate Democrats will choose their leader for the new Congress, which begins in January. No date for the vote had been announced.

title: Tinubu Condemns Violence at Campaign Events Ahead of 2027
dek: The president told security agencies to deal firmly with political thuggery and said rivals "are not enemies".
body: President Bola Tinubu on Friday, 13 November, condemned rising violence at political events and warned politicians and their supporters against using the 2027 campaigns to intimidate or attack opponents.

"Every form of violence stands condemned," he said, adding that violence should never have a place in political campaigns. He repeated an earlier order for security agencies to confront thuggery and other anti-democratic acts firmly.

Tinubu told parties and candidates they are free to campaign anywhere in the country without harassment. He described political rivals as members of "the same household living in different rooms" and restated his commitment to free and fair elections.

title: Starship Reaches Orbit on Flight 15, but SpaceX Skips the Booster Catch
dek: The ship deployed 26 Starlink satellites. The Super Heavy booster splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico instead of returning to the tower.
body: SpaceX launched its 15th Starship test flight from Starbase in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET on 13 November. The ship reached low Earth orbit and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites.

The planned catch of the Super Heavy booster by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms was called off. The booster made a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico instead, and SpaceX did not immediately explain why.
The ship was set to orbit Earth 14 times over more than 21 hours, with a possible tower catch of the upper stage on 14 November if engineers judged it safe.

title: YouTube Is Coming Back to the Billboard Charts in 2027
dek: Billboard is narrowing the gap between paid and free streams, and YouTube says that is enough to bring its data back.
body: Billboard is changing how it counts streams. On its album and song charts, a paid stream will now be worth 1.5 ad-supported streams, down from 2.5. The change starts with the charts dated 16 January 2027.

YouTube stopped sending its US data to Billboard in January 2026 after an earlier formula change, arguing that it undervalued free listening. Its streams have been missing from the charts since the end of January.
YouTube has now confirmed it will rejoin the US charts in 2027. Its music chief, Lyor Cohen, said the new method better reflects how fans listen on both paid and free services.

title: CAF Awards Head to Lagos as Super Eagles Miss the Team Shortlist
dek: Nigeria's National Theatre hosts African football's awards night on 7 December.
body: The 2026 CAF Awards will be held on 7 December at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, the National Theatre in Lagos.

Nigeria was left off the 10-team shortlist for Men's National Team of the Year, despite finishing third at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. The nominees are Algeria, Cape Verde, Ivory Coast, DR Congo, Egypt, Ghana, Morocco, Senegal, South Africa and Tunisia, the 10 African teams that played at the 2026 World Cup.
Nigeria missed the World Cup after losing a playoff to DR Congo on penalties.

title: Norris Wins a Wild Brazilian Grand Prix as Mercedes Seal the Constructors' Title
dek: Mercedes won their first constructors' championship since 2021. Verstappen and Hadjar completed the podium.
body: Lando Norris won the Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos on 8 November in changing wet and dry conditions. It was the McLaren driver's third win of 2026.
Max Verstappen finished second, 14.6 seconds back, and his Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar was third.
George Russell (fourth) and Kimi Antonelli (fifth) scored enough points to give Mercedes the constructors' championship, their ninth and first since 2021. The Las Vegas Grand Prix is next.

title: COP31 Opens in Antalya With a Focus on Delivering Climate Promises
dek: Nearly 200 countries are meeting in Türkiye until 20 November. Climate finance for developing countries is high on the agenda.
body: The UN climate conference COP31 opened in Antalya, Türkiye, on 9 November and runs until 20 November. Nearly 200 countries are taking part, and more than 90,000 people are expected.
Türkiye's environment minister, Murat Kurum, is COP31 president. Australia's Chris Bowen oversees the negotiations under a co-presidency agreed at COP30.

Rather than chasing a single landmark deal, this summit focuses on turning existing pledges into action. Key issues include faster access to climate finance for developing countries, clean energy, adaptation and preparing for a strong El Niño.

title: EU Proposes Rules to Rein In Dark Patterns and Hard-to-Cancel Subscriptions
dek: The Digital Fairness Act targets addictive design, confusing prices and free trials that quietly become paid subscriptions.
body: The European Commission proposed the Digital Fairness Act on 11 November, a set of consumer rules aimed at manipulative design online.

The proposal targets dark patterns, addictive features, unclear or changing prices, exploitative personalisation and online contracts that are hard to cancel. Examples include free trials that turn into paid subscriptions and cancel buttons hidden deep in menus.
It is a proposal for now, and its wording may change as the European Parliament and member states negotiate it.

title: Tech Stocks Slip on Nvidia Turmoil as Bitcoin Drops Below $70,000
dek: Producer prices rose 6.5% over the past year, and traders are betting on a Fed rate hike in December.
body: The Nasdaq and the S&P 500 closed lower on Friday, 13 November, as Nvidia's leadership crisis weighed on technology shares.

US producer prices rose 0.3% in October, slightly below forecasts, but were up 6.5% from a year earlier, the biggest annual rise since November 2022. Markets are pricing in a quarter-point interest rate hike at the Federal Reserve's 8 to 9 December meeting.
Bitcoin fell below $70,000 for the first time since August, trading around $68,900, and more than $1.3 billion in crypto futures positions were liquidated in 24 hours. Gold held near $3,894 an ounce.

title: Canada and Major AI Companies Sign a Voluntary AI Safety Declaration
dek: Anthropic, Cohere, Microsoft, Mistral AI and OpenAI are among the signatories committing to incident reporting and shared safety standards.
body: Canada signed a joint declaration on AI safety and security on 9 November, joining Bahrain, Finland, France, Norway and the Netherlands.

AI companies including Anthropic, Cohere, Microsoft, Mistral AI and OpenAI also signed. The declaration covers clearer rules, reporting of serious incidents, risk management, shared evaluation standards and early-warning channels for serious AI and cybersecurity incidents.
It is voluntary. It does not create new law or set penalties.
